data.narrative:
New Limit is a Series C biotech company that has raised $610M+ and carries a last post-money valuation of $3.1B. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 11 comparable companies across Biotech & Health: 3 public equities (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private firms including Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B Series C), Chai Discovery ($3.8B Series C), and public-stage peers Recursion Pharmaceuticals ($1.6B), Freenome ($1.1B), and Alto Neuroscience ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods prove applicable. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $5.3B. The peer-median method across five same-sector comparables produces $1.6B, reflecting substantial dispersion in the biotech universe (range $1.0B–$10.3B). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples cannot be applied due to absent revenue disclosure, common for private companies. The median peer valuation of $1.6B falls materially below New Limit's last post-money, suggesting either premium positioning or valuation inflation relative to disclosed peers.

The triangulated range spans $1.4B (low) to $6.1B (high) with a median of $3.4B. The current $3.1B valuation sits near the median, supported by stage-progression logic but substantially above peer medians. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of selected peers, undisclosed revenue or clinical progress metrics, and whether premium valuations reflect genuine differentiation or market cyclicality in frontier biotech.
